questions.topic: eGurukul · Drugs Acting on Ganglia & Anti Smoking Drugs
questions.stem: A 15-year-old boy started smoking his first cigarette. Which Of the following effects was most likely elicited by nicotine soon after smoking?

options.label: B
options.text: Dilation of the skin and splanchnic vessels

options.label: C
options.text: Increased epinephrine secretion from the adrenal Medulla

questions.answerText: Increased epinephrine secretion from the adrenal Medulla
questions.solutionHtml:
Increased epinephrine secretion from the adrenal Medulla

Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number: 133-134

questions.topic: eGurukul · Drugs Acting on Ganglia & Anti Smoking Drugs
questions.stem: A 26-year-old man presented to her physician complaining that he felt fearful, helpless, and worried almost continuously during the day. The history of the patient indicated that he was a difficult child to manage and often impulsive And unproductive in school. he started smoking at the age of 17 and now smoked two packs of cigarettes daily. He tried to quit smoking several times with no success. The Physician suggested trying a drug that was effective in treating both depressive and attention deficit disorders, as well as In smoking cessation. Which of the following drugs was most likely prescribed?
questions.solutionHtml:
Bupropion
  • Bupropion is an antidepressant that was also found to be effective in treating attention deficit hyperactivity disorder and is approved as an adjunct in the management of smoking cessation. Because the patient has symptoms of both depression and ADHD and wants to quit smoking, bupropion can be an appropriate drug.


Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number: 490-491

questions.topic: eGurukul · Drugs Acting on Ganglia & Anti Smoking Drugs
questions.stem: A 30-year-old woman smoker expresses a desire to Quit smoking. She has a 10-pack-year history of smoking but no other health issues. She wants to try varenicline, a drug she recently heard about, to help her Quit. Which of the following side effects of varenicline Is she most likely to encounter?
questions.solutionHtml:
Abnormal dreams
  • Varenicline is thought to decrease nicotine cravings by stimulating neuronal nicotinic acetylcholine receptors (nAChRs). This provides a moderate level of stimulation in place of nicotine, making quitting easier. It also blocks the full effects of nicotine by competing with the binding sites in cases where a patient on varenicline does smoke. These occur in about 10% of patients.


Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number: 134

questions.topic: eGurukul · Drugs Acting on Ganglia & Anti Smoking Drugs
questions.stem: Which of the following statements is correct about the normal functioning of the nicotinic receptors in a 19-year-old male college student-athlete from the College baseball team?

options.label: A
options.text: Nicotine at high doses stimulates the receptor

options.label: B
options.text: Nicotinic receptors are located in the adrenal cortex

options.label: C
options.text: Nicotinic receptors are located in the autonomic Ganglia

options.label: D
options.text: Nicotinic receptors located at the neuromuscular Junction are known as NN receptors

questions.answerText: Nicotinic receptors are located in the autonomic Ganglia
questions.solutionHtml:
Nicotinic receptors are located in the autonomic Ganglia
  • Nicotinic receptors are located in the autonomic ganglia. Nicotine at low concentrations stimulates the receptor and at high concentration blocks the receptor.
  • Nicotinic receptors are located in the CNS, adrenal medulla, autonomic ganglia, and the neuromuscular junction (NMJ).
  • Those at the NMJ are sometimes designated NM and the others, NN.
  • The nicotinic receptors of autonomic ganglia differ from those of the NMJ. For example, ganglionic receptors are selectively blocked by hexamethonium, whereas NMJ receptors are specifically blocked by tubocurarine.


Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number: 133-134
